$comment: OMN-17942. The admission vocabulary for a Linear issue CREATE.
Read by plugins/onex/hooks/lib/ticket_creation_guard.py, which is invoked
by the pre_tool_use_ticket_creation_gate.sh PreToolUse hook. The vocabulary
lives here, not in the checker, so changing admission policy is a config
edit visible in one place rather than a rule a reader has to infer from a
Python literal.
JSON rather than YAML deliberately, matching agent_model_allowlist.json in
this directory: the checker sits on a fail-closed enforcement path, so it
parses its own policy with the standard library alone. A missing PyYAML in
the resolved interpreter would otherwise turn into a refusal of every
Linear write on the machine.
There is deliberately NO escape entry -- no 'any', no wildcard criterion,
no 'exempt' marker. An unbound ticket is the defect this guard refuses, and
a sanctioned spelling for it is a sanctioned incident.
prd_source -- the exact revision criterion_ids and invariant_ids were read
from. The vocabulary is sourced from a document in ANOTHER repository, so
'the ids come from the PRD' is an uncheckable claim without naming the
revision. tests/hooks/test_ticket_creation_guard.py reads the file at this
commit and at origin/main and fails on either drift, skipping with a
stated reason when no clone of that private repo is present (this repo's
CI runners do not clone it). Bump commit, criterion_ids and invariant_ids
in ONE change: a vocabulary that lags its source admits bindings to
commitments the document no longer makes, and refuses the ones it does.
criterion_ids -- the release-criterion identifiers a Gate line may cite.
C1..C27, the rows of section 6 of the beta PRD. This gate first shipped
bound to C1..C6 from beta/plans/customer-plane-validation-charter-plan.md
because the PRD then existed only on a draft PR and no C-id enumeration
was reachable at origin/main; knowledge-base-internal#125 merged to main
as cac690c3 and the enumeration now exists, so the charter is no longer a
source. INV-109 rules the customer-plane validation probes tests rather
than ship conditions, so a charter probe id is not a commitment a ticket
can bind to. No charter id had to be DROPPED: the PRD table spells
C1..C27, which covers all six charter spellings -- what changed is what
each id RESOLVES to, not whether the string is admitted.
invariant_ids -- the invariant identifiers a Gate line may cite. These are
the 42 entries of the PRD's machine-readable invariant-coverage block,
NOT every INV- token in the document. The PRD deliberately declines the
deploy and security scopes while citing individual invariants from them
by reference (INV-032, INV-071..INV-074, INV-086), and its section 9.2
names INV-108 as process-scoped and carried by a different document.
Binding a ticket to an id the PRD only mentions would bind it to a
commitment this document does not make, which is the defect this gate
exists to refuse.
epic_markers -- an issue with no parentId is admitted only if its
description carries one of these as a LINE OF ITS OWN, matched exactly
after trimming and lowercasing. Substring matching is refused on purpose
(omni_home CLAUDE.md rule 15): a gate that matches anywhere in the body
passes on prose that merely mentions the marker, including prose that
mentions it in order to deny it. Prefix matching is refused for a second
reason -- a line reading 'Epic: OMN-16729' NAMES a parent epic, and under
a prefix rule the ticket most tightly bound to a parent would be the one
admitted as parentless.
in_progress_state_names -- the state names/types that mean WORK IN FLIGHT.
Rule 5 fires only on a create that names one of these, matched exactly
after trimming and lowercasing against 'state', 'stateId', 'status' and
'statusType'. 'started' is Linear's state TYPE for the in-progress band,
so a create naming the type rather than the state is caught too. A raw
uuid is deliberately NOT matched: this guard has no workspace lookup and
refusing on an id it cannot resolve would make every id-shaped create
unfileable. That is the one fail-OPEN direction in this policy and it is
bounded to rule 5.
residual_title_terms -- title shapes that read as work spun out of other
work rather than work bound to a commitment. Matched on word boundaries,
so 'minor' does not fire on 'minority' and 'nit' does not fire on
'monitor'. A residual belongs as a comment on its parent; the standing
rule is 'do not file follow-up tickets for residuals -- comment on the
parent'. The single exemption is a live-gate defect, because a gate
reporting green while enforcing nothing is not a residual, and burying it
in a comment thread is how it stays unfixed.

prd_source.invariant_ids_from: the invariant-coverage HTML-comment block in the front matter
